outcome.a_remember: Petar brought a loaf, said mill still broken, may be fixed next week. Quarry not hiring until month turns. He admitted mainland flour doesn't hold well, then asked about council meeting. I agreed to trade soup for bread and keep quiet about the flour rumor.

insights: I've got a job at the inn and a place to sleep, so I've planted my feet on the first day.
Petar's the mayor and he's got troubles with the mill and quarry, but he still came through with that loaf — that's the kind of connection that matters.
I keep a ledger in my head of who owes what, and Petar owes me a loaf until he brings it, but my lips are sealed about his flour.
intentions: Work a shift at the inn tomorrow and see who comes through, so I can learn more names.
Ask Petar about the council meeting when I see him, because he brought it up and I want to know what's happening.
Keep gathering gossip about the mill and the quarry, so I can be the one who knows the town's business.

opinions.opinion: He's a bit gruff and secretive, but he kept his word about the loaf and trusts me with the mainland flour thing. He's someone worth knowing.

projects.title: Make the inn the heart of town
projects.why: I want the inn to be where people gather, and I've started by working here and getting to know the regulars like Petar.

projects.title: Keep track of who owes whom
projects.why: My secret ledger of debts helps me understand everyone's place in town, and I've already noted Petar's loaf and his flour secret.

self.advice: Trust the people who keep their word, but keep a ledger of what they owe.
self.fear: Being left out of the town's news and shifts.
self.strangers: Warm and quick to learn a name, but I hold back the details until I know them.
self.summary: I'm Rosa Vidal, back on the island where I grew up, working the inn and remembering that a town runs on bread and secrets.
self.want: To make this inn the center of town, one bowl of soup at a time.

output.summary: Today I stepped off the boat with 40 coins and found my place. I got taken on as help at the inn, which suits me, and I talked with Petar Ilić twice — that man's the mayor, though he's moaning about the mill and the quarry. He brought me a loaf like he said, even if it's a bit stale, and he told me to keep quiet about him buying mainland flour. I kept my word. I bought bread for myself twice and ate it, and I walked to the council hall and the market, but town stays quiet on Sunday. I've got 38 coins left, two nights paid at the inn, and a job. I meant to ask around at the harbor and take a dock shift today, but I got caught up at the inn and with Petar, so those steps missed. That's fine. I'm in no rush. I've got my ledger in my head, and I'm watching who comes and goes.
